$comment: Sources-of-law hierarchy as DATA. rank_order lists source types from highest to lowest authority for the lex-superior defeater (jurisdiction-general shape: supranational primary law over supranational secondary law over national law, constitution first, descending to administrative acts). ranks assigns the numeric rank the solver's Norm.rank carries (higher wins); the gaps leave room for jurisdiction-specific insertions without renumbering. Conflict RESOLUTION is not encoded here and not implemented in this package: the solver's LEX_CONFLICT_PACK applies lex-superior (rank) then lex-specialis (specificity) then lex-posterior (time). specificity and time are per-provision facts supplied by the caller, per the notes.

notes.specificity: lex specialis: a per-provision fact, not a source-type property — a provision addressing a narrower class of cases carries a higher specificity value; equal-rank conflicts separate on it second.
notes.time: lex posterior: the provision's enactment date as a monotonic integer (e.g. ISO date digits 20180525); equal-rank, equal-specificity conflicts separate on it last. Later wins.
notes.escalation: two provisions equal on rank, specificity, and time are a GENUINE collision — the solver reports the act 'open' and the conflict escalates; nothing here fabricates a winner.
